summary: This manuscript establishes four major, transcendental-free structural refinements and impossibility barriers for computing normal-form correlated equilibria (NFCE) in extensive-form games. By introducing a rational two-bin Cauchy-Schwarz decoding technique, the author sharpens gadget parameters by 8x/64x, proves robust PPAD-completeness for inverse-polynomial approximation error, sharpens uniform linear programming gaps while proving exponential decay necessity, and fully characterizes universal node-based totality and subquadratic-slack complexity. All results are rigorously verified via both a constructive Lean 4 formalization and an exact-rational Python certificate suite.
strengths: Replaces transcendental entropy, logarithms, and Pinsker's inequality with a sharp, purely rational two-bin Cauchy-Schwarz partition over Q.
Achieves an exact 8x reduction in gadget parameter m and 64x in support bound kappa_d, significantly tightening the algorithmic framework of Cheval et al. (2026).
Extends PPAD-completeness from exact equilibria to inverse-polynomial approximate delta-NFCE at delta = Theta(|V|^-8/3) and Theta(|V|^-5/2).
Constructs an explicit {0,1}-payoff bimatrix family proving that exponential LP gap decay 2^-Omega(|S|) is genuinely unavoidable.
Fully machine-checked in constructive Lean 4.36.0 with zero sorry and complemented by a zero-float exact-rational Python verification suite.
weaknesses: The exposition is exceptionally dense and mathematically demanding, requiring deep familiarity with sequence-form sparsification and extensive-form game theory.
Certain gadget constructions and parameter choices involve intricate algebraic bounds that, while fully verified, are complex to navigate.
